desc:
Connecting payments, a CRM and email to your app turns separate tools into one working system. Ecom Swift LLC wires services such as Stripe, HubSpot and your email provider into your own code through their official APIs, with safe key storage, retries and tested flows.

## What is a custom integration?

A custom integration is code that lets your product exchange data with an outside service. When a customer pays, your app tells your records. When someone signs up, your CRM receives the contact. When an order ships, an email goes out. Each of these links needs authentication, a defined set of messages and a plan for what happens when the other service is slow or down.

## Why manual copying between tools costs you

Without integrations, someone copies details from one screen to another. Signups sit in a spreadsheet until Friday. Payments are matched to accounts by hand. Welcome emails go out late or never. Each manual step is a chance for a typo, a missed customer or a delay that the buyer notices.

Badly built integrations are worse than none. A payment webhook that is never checked can be forged. An API key written into the code can leak. A call that fails once and is never retried quietly loses a customer record. Integration work is mostly about handling the unhappy path properly.

## How connected services affect revenue and workload

Connected tools shorten the time between a customer's action and your response. A new lead appears in your CRM within moments, so your team can reply while interest is high. A paid invoice unlocks access automatically, so the customer is not left waiting. Analytics events show which steps people complete, which feeds better decisions.

The savings are in hours and mistakes. Staff stop re-entering data, reports draw from one source of truth, and your product behaves like a finished service instead of a set of manual favors.

## What a great integration includes

- The service's official API or SDK, not unofficial workarounds.
- API keys and secrets stored in secure environment settings.
- Webhooks that are received, verified and processed once, even if the service sends them twice.
- Retries with sensible waiting times when a call fails.
- Clear error handling that records what went wrong and for which customer.
- An email alert when a link breaks, so failures are not silent.
- Tests with sample data, including failed payments and missing fields.
- Two way sync where the service supports it and your process needs it.
- A sync log screen in your admin area for larger setups.
- A setup guide that explains each key, setting and endpoint.

## What we do

We list the services you want connected and the events that should pass between them. Then we build each link, test it with sample data and write a short guide. The Basic package connects one service. Standard connects two, adds webhooks, retries, error alerts and a team setup guide. Premium connects up to four, adds a logged sync history in your admin, automated tests for each link and a code walkthrough.

Payment details are handled by the payment provider's own hosted tools, so card numbers are never stored in your code.

## What to do, and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Create the service accounts yourself, so you own them.
- Use test mode or sandbox keys while we build.
- Decide which system is the source of truth for each type of data.
- Tell us which events matter, such as refunds and cancellations.
- Keep an inventory of every service your product depends on.

**Avoid:**
- Pasting secret keys into chat, email or the code itself.
- Syncing every field when you only use a few.
- Ignoring failed webhook deliveries.
- Switching to live keys before the full flow is tested.
- Connecting five services at once before one works well.

## Who this is for

This service suits a membership site that needs paid sign ups to create accounts automatically. It suits a sales team that wants form leads in HubSpot without copying them. It also suits a store owner who wants order data to reach a spreadsheet and a mailing list.

## What we need from you

Tell us which services to connect and what should happen between them. Create the accounts and share developer access to the services and to your code repository as a collaborator. Please never send passwords. We will tell you where to place keys yourself. After you order, we send a short checklist and keep you updated until every link is tested.
